title: Trace-driven hypothesis notebook for latency outliers
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for trace-driven hypotheses around sporadic tail latency/outliers for inference requests. Intended audience: oncall, SREs, and engineers owning runtime and routing logic. Use it during an active investigation or to structure postmortems.

Quick summary / tl;dr:
- Problem: intermittent 95th+ latency spikes affecting small fraction of requests (0.5%–2%) with no obvious CPU/GPU saturation.
- Working hypothesis vector set: (A) cold/partial KV cache misses with long disk swap; (B) routing to fallback model variants with different init paths; (C) throttled downstream I/O (metrics service, auth); (D) noisy neighbors on host-level kernel scheduling.
- This notebook maps signals (metrics + traces) to concrete checks and dashboard widgets to accelerate root cause identification.

Context / background notes:
- Spike profile: short (30–300s), often correlated with increased burstiness of long-sequence prompts. Seen most frequently in eu-west-1, but not exclusive.
- Instrumentation caveat: some internal spans omit tenant_id for privacy; we use session_id and hashed route for stitching. Ensure redaction policy is respected when copying traces.

Key metrics (definitions + rationale):
1) request.latency.p50/p90/p95/p99 (ms) — end-to-end api gateway to response. Primary SLI.
2) kv.prefix.cache.hit_ratio (percent) — per-model and per-tenant. Low hit_ratio on a tenant during spike supports hypothesis A.
3) model.init.duration (ms) — time spent in model bootstrap paths (loading quantized weights into memory, compilation). High values implicate fallback/model-switch.
4) host.cpu.steal_pct and host.load1 — host scheduling pressure; noisy neighbor indicator.
5) grpc.downstream.call.duration and error_rate — check for downstream auth/metadata services adding tail latency.
6) kernel-swap.rate and disk.io.ps — used if KV cache unexpectedly falls to disk.
7) serving.kv.disk-read-ms.percentile — distribution of disk reads from KV layer.
8) routing.fallback.count and routing.variant.latency — count of times request routed to fallback and latencies for each variant.

Recommended trace anchors and span naming (conventions):
- api.gateway.receive -> span:gateway.receive (attrs: route, method, tenant_hash, session_id)
- router.evaluate -> span:router.eval (attrs: policy, candidate_models, fallback_flag)
- kv.lookup -> span:kv.lookup (attrs: key_prefix, hit_bool, backend:mem|disk)
- model.init -> span:model.init (attrs: model_name, quantized:bool, compilation:bool)
- runtime.generate -> span:runtime.generate (attrs: batch_size, seq_len, kv_cache_present:bool)
- network.call -> span:net.call (attrs: host, service, rtt_ms)
- response.serialize -> span:response.serialize (attrs: bytes_out)

Span tag guidance (fields to ensure present):
- session_id (short hash)
- tenant_hash (PII-safe)
- route_id (API route)
- model_variant
- kv_backend (mem, sharedmem, disk)
- node_id / host_id

Trace-driven investigation script (cheat sequence):
1) Identify time window of spike: use request.latency.p95 heatmap to find cluster.
2) Pull raw traces (sampled) for that window with filter: session_id NOT null AND request.latency > p95_threshold.
3) Run fast aggregation on traces to group by root cause candidates: group by kv_backend, routing.fallback, model.init.duration > 200ms.
4) If kv_backend==disk frequently, check serving.kv.disk-read-ms.percentile and host.disk.io.
5) If model.init present, correlate model.init.duration with routing.variant and directory of model artifacts (hot cache vs cold).
6) Cross-check host.cpu.steal_pct for nodes hosting high-latency traces.
7) Inspect grpc.downstream.call.duration within the same trace for spikes.

Example PromQL queries to attach to dashboard widgets:
- p95 latency by route:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- KV hit ratio per model:
  sum(rate(kv_hits_total[5m])) by (model) / sum(rate(kv_requests_total[5m])) by (model)
- Model init time distribution:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(model_init_duration_bucket[10m])) by (le, model))
- Count of fallback routes:
  sum(rate(routing_fallback_total[5m])) by (route, model_variant)

Dashboard wireframe ideas (compact investigation-focused panels):
- Top row: p95/p99 latency (global) + request rate + error rate (short window selectable)
- Middle: Heatmap of p95 by route x time (identify routes that spike)
- Middle-right: KV telemetry panel: hit ratio, disk-read-ms p95, active insert rate
- Bottom-left: Trace-sample quick-links: list of sampled traces with one-click open to full trace viewer (session_id column)
- Bottom-right: Node pressure panel: host.cpu.steal_pct, load1, kernel-swap.rate.
- Slide-up debug toolbox: canned PromQL snippets + quick curl commands to reproduce/force path

Hypotheses and rapid checks (structured):
- Hypothesis A: cold KV cache causing disk reads -> check kv_backend==disk in traces, disk-read-ms p95 > 50ms, kv.hit_ratio drop. Quick probe: replay recent session_id on a node with warm cache and compare end-to-end latency.
- Hypothesis B: routing to fallback triggers model.init slow path -> check routing.fallback.count spikes; look for model.init spans and their durations. Quick probe: force routing policy locally to ensure candidate_model order reversed and run synthetic probe with sequence length similar to observed.
- Hypothesis C: downstream auth/metadata adds latency -> inspect grpc.downstream.call spans in same trace and correlate with external-service latency metrics. Quick probe: simulate downstream failure and see amplified tail.
- Hypothesis D: kernel scheduling/noisy neighbor -> correlate host.cpu.steal_pct, container cpu throttling (cgroup throttling metrics) and long runtime.generate spans. Quick probe: migrate a hot tenant to an isolated host and re-run traffic.

Automated alert ideas (short-term):
- Alert if p99 latency increases by >2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1m buckets AND fallback.count increases > 50% relative to last 30m.
- Alert on kv.disk-read-ms.p95 > 80ms for any model with request rate > 10 rps.

Investigation playbook checklist (for oncall):
- [ ] Grab time window, note affected routes and tenant hashes (PII-safe).
- [ ] Pull 50 traces (sampled) for that window and run the script above.
- [ ] Check kv metrics and model init metrics at node granularity.
- [ ] If host signals present, escalate to infra with host_id and trace links.
- [ ] If fallback problem found, open a ticket: include trace IDs, model_variant, and exact timestamp.

Notes for telemetry engineering (instrumentation gaps):
- Missing: explicit kv_backend tag on older KV client versions. Add migration plan and compatibility check.
- Missing: per-span node_id in some model.init spans; add node_id attribute or ensure trace hops include a node_id tag.
- Suggested: add a short-lived 'investigation' metric recording trace_count_by_hypothesis label to make aggregated dashboards faster.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why does eu-west-1 show higher incidence? Possible load pattern differences or artifact placement. Need to check model artifact distribution and cold-start patterns across regions.
- Are long-sequence prompts disproportionately using a code path that invalidates KV cache? Need sampling of prompt lengths attached to traces (privacy review required).

Next steps / action items:
- Telemetry eng: add kv_backend tag + node_id to model.init spans (owner: Priya) — due 2026-03-10.
- SRE: create temporary p95 alert tying fallback.count and latency (owner: Benji) — due 2026-03-03.
- Runtime eng: reproduce model.init cold-start locally with quantized models and measure model.init.duration (owner: Luis) — due 2026-03-07.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Trace export (internal tooling): rtv export --start "2026-02-19T15:40:00Z" --end "2026-02-19T15:50:00Z" --filter "latency>500" --out traces.json
- Quick curl to internal probe endpoint (example): curl -s -X POST https://int-probe.redwood/route/test -d '{"prompt":"<long-seq>"}' -H "x-test-session: debug-123"

References and links:
- Related convos: slack:#obs-investigations thread 2026-02-19 (see pinned)
- Telemetry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/189
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-4723 (tail-latency incident tracker)

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc lightweight — convert to a formal runbook if a recurring pattern emerges.
- When adding metrics, prefer short-term derivable signals (low-cardinality) for alerting, keep high-cardinality fields for drilldown only.

-- end of notebook --
